title: Rigveda 10.135: The boy and the wagon
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.135: The boy and the wagon: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.135 is a hymn of 7 verses addressed to the boy and the wagon. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 123v-124r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.135.1-3 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 7, varga 23); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 123v
translation.original_text:
1yasmi̍n vṛ̱kṣe su̍palā̱śe de̱vaiḥ sa̱mpiba̍te ya̱maḥ | atrā̍ no vi̱śpati̍ḥ pi̱tā pu̍rā̱ṇām̐ anu̍ venati ||
2pu̱rā̱ṇām̐ a̍nu̱vena̍nta̱ṁ cara̍ntam pā̱payā̍mu̱yā | a̱sū̱yann a̱bhy a̍cākaśa̱ṁ tasmā̍ aspṛhaya̱m puna̍ḥ ||
3yaṁ ku̍māra̱ nava̱ṁ ratha̍m aca̱kram mana̱sākṛ̍ṇoḥ | eke̍ṣaṁ vi̱śvata̱ḥ prāñca̱m apa̍śya̱nn adhi̍ tiṣṭhasi ||
translation.text:
1IN the Tree clothed with goodly leaves where Yama drinketh with the Gods, The Father, Master of the house, tendeth with love our ancient Sires.
2I looked reluctantly on him who cherishes those men of old, On him who treads that evil path, and then I yearned for this again.
3Thou mountest, though thou dost not see, O Child, the new and wheel-less car Which thou hast fashioned mentally, onepoled but turning every way.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 123v (OPenn image 123, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.134.6 ‹-padājo vayāṁ yathā yamo›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 124r, begins in RV 10.135.4 ‹-prāvartata sam ito nāvy›. Verses 10.135.1-3 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.135.4-7 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 7, varga 23); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 124r
translation.original_text:
4yaṁ ku̍māra̱ prāva̍rtayo̱ ratha̱ṁ vipre̍bhya̱s pari̍ | taṁ sāmānu̱ prāva̍rtata̱ sam i̱to nā̱vy āhi̍tam ||
5kaḥ ku̍mā̱ram a̍janaya̱d ratha̱ṁ ko nir a̍vartayat | kaḥ svi̱t tad a̱dya no̍ brūyād anu̱deyī̱ yathābha̍vat ||
6yathābha̍vad anu̱deyī̱ tato̱ agra̍m ajāyata | pu̱rastā̍d bu̱dhna āta̍taḥ pa̱ścān ni̱raya̍ṇaṁ kṛ̱tam ||
7i̱daṁ ya̱masya̱ sāda̍naṁ devamā̱naṁ yad u̱cyate̍ | i̱yam a̍sya dhamyate nā̱ḻīr a̱yaṁ gī̱rbhiḥ pari̍ṣkṛtaḥ ||
translation.text:
4The car which thou hast made to roll hitherward from the Sages, Child! This hath the Sâman followed close, hence, laid together on a ship.
5Who was the father of the child? Who made the chariot roll away? Who will this day declare to us how the funeral gift was made?
6When the funeral gift was placed, straightway the point of flame appeared. A depth extended in the front: a passage out was made behind.
7Here is the seat where Yama dwells, that which is called the Home of Gods: Here minstrels blow the flute for him here he is glorified with songs.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 124r (OPenn image 123, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.135.4 ‹-prāvartata sam ito nāvy›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 124v, begins in RV 10.136.2 ‹-devāso avikṣata›. Verses 10.135.4-7 end on this page; 10.135.4 begins on fol. 123v.
